In the youth's events John Martin has been outstanding. He is one of the few athletes who will have a go at nearly anything and has often wanted to compete in youth, junior and senior events on the same day.

The youths section is definitely the strongest it has ever been,with a whole host of budding stars.Performances by J.Vivian,A.Major and John Martin, ably supported by many others,overshadow some of our seniors' efforts.

Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major. Many others who are under the guidance of Tom Carter are improving fast and the seniors will surely benefit in the very near future.

A cold day greeted our first track meeting at Battersea Park on 24th April, but what a fine start by Cliff Brooks and field events captain John Martin in the Shot Putt, both producing personal bests, over 40 feet and there is little doubt that even better performances are in store.
But pride of place undoubtedly went to the shot-putt, where Cliff shoved the benefit of technique training with a distance of 41' 4½", and John Martin was also over 40'.
John Martin was just under 40' in the shot-putt, while the question on everyone's lips after the long-jump was: Has Belgrave at last produced its answer to Bob Beamon?

Also selected for the senior events was John Martin - a fitting reward for his recent improvement. In the under-18 events, the Bels came out with two winners, Mick Marshall being timed at a wind-assisted 10.9s. in the 100m., and Martin Bloice at 29.7s. in the 250m.

An Inter-Club meeting at Chiswick on the last day of May saw the Bel's turn out in force in the 800m to show what depth we have in this event. A battle royal went on between John Martin and Dave McMillan for third and fourth place; & shotputter John just won.
But Mick Marshall, John Martin and Reg Hopkins, Jr., were all winners in the "B" string events, and in tying for second place, with Luton, behind the Police, we were not disgraced.
When John Martin wins the triple jump, it is a fair bet that Belgrave are set for a team victory.

Steve White got a good hat-trick, in the 100m., 200m., and long-jump, however, while John Martin took the shot, discus, and (unlikely story) the high-jump with a personal best of 5' 2", and failed to add a fourth title, in the javelin, by just 2cm.
In the 110m. hurdles championship, Willie Williams, out junior high jump champion, won his first senior title, with a narrow victory over John Martin, our shot, discus and senior high jump champion.
Those indefatigable field events twins John Martin and Bill Couzens carried our colours in the field. John was second in the shot, with 11.28m., and Bill Couzens third with 9.73m.

John Martin deputised in both hurdle events and did a great job, especially in the 400m hurdles. Steve White and Jim Vivian, who we were very pleased to see back on the track this year, both completed sprint doubles and Charlie Gillett won both the 400m hurdles and the 400m 'B' race.
